To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

microdialysis was applied to measure extracellular VEGFA in situ in breast cancer tumors and normal adjacent tissue in breast cancer patients and that there is a significant positive correlation in normal tissue between extracellular VEGFa and estradiol, while there is no correlation between tumor VEGFa and plasma VEGFa or between estradiol levels and tumor VEGFa.

1) microdialysis can be used to sample extracellular VEG in situ in human breast tumors; 2) VEG is significantly elevated in tumors compared with adjacent normal breast tissue; 3) estradiol correlates with extracellular VEG levels in normal breast tissue; and 4) estradiol is elevated in tumors compared to adjacent normal breast tissue.

Microdialysis is a technique that enables the in vivo sampling of extracellular angiogenic molecules, and in this study, we have shown that VEGF levels are elevated in breast cancer tissue compared to normal tissue and that there is a correlation between VEGF and estrogen levels in the extracellular fluid of normal breast tissue, but not in tumors.

the development of a new technology, microdialysis, for sampling of angiogenic factors in situ, and we have demonstrated that this technique may be applicable in breast cancer.
